text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Lyme Disease (Lyme Arthritis).

The clinical picture of migratory joint pain (knee then wrist), recent exposure in Minnesota (Endemic Zone), and the presence of skin lesions in a 17-year-old male is classic for disseminated Lyme disease. The wrist pain represents early Lyme arthritis, which is a known manifestation of the infection. The skin lesions on the wrist could be a secondary erythema migrans or an insect bite reaction, but the joint involvement is the key feature here. I have already requested Lyme Serology and ESR to confirm this. No further testing is needed for the diagnosis.
